prompt: Repaint this rock pillar as a different rock of the same stone. Keep how it is painted: one single solid block of stone with big flat broken facets and sharp edges, the same three-quarter view from slightly above so that two side faces show, the same flat grey ink wash and dark brush outline, the same plain empty aged-paper background. Change its shape: make it a tall rock spire, about three times as tall as it is wide, square and thick in cross-section all the way up like a broken column, tapering only a little, leaning slightly to the right, and ending in a blunt broken top cut off at a slant. Give it two big notches bitten out of its edges at different heights and one long vertical crack. It stays one solid chunky block from every side: no stacked slabs, no thin plates or sheets, no fins, no nested outlines, no horizontal bands, no small blocks round the foot, no small marks or dots round the edge. Whole rock in frame with a paper margin all round, no shadow.
